item.title: The fight between Santa Barbara County and Sable oil: What happens next? - Santa Barbara News-Press
item.description: Local authorities, state officials, and area environmentalists ramp up challenges to new crude oil now moving across Santa Barbara County

item.title: The Rack, Santa Barbara’s only family-friendly pool hall, is now open - Santa Barbara News-Press
item.description: The pool hall caters to a variety of skill levels and competitiveness. While being open for casual play, the hall also offers tournaments and leagues to compete in as well as a place for individuals to practice

item.title: Commentary: What Cesar Chavez cost the movement - Santa Barbara News-Press
item.description: History shows us that organizers, workers and advocates solved problems by coming together, not by blindly following orders from Cesar Chavez.

item.title: California’s wealthiest lawmakers are heavily invested in the stock market - Santa Barbara News-Press
item.description: More than half of the lawmakers representing California have a median net worth of at least $1 million.

item.title: Manifattura gains traction on lower State Street with a craft-driven culinary concept - Santa Barbara News-Press
item.description: A tightly edited menu, understated showmanship and dishes approached with an artistic sensibility define the restaurant’s early momentum

item.title: As fiber optic broadband future nears, will all of Santa Barbara County benefit? - Santa Barbara News-Press
item.description: Time will tell if the advantages of next-generation high speed internet extend to the Cuyama Valley, where access to broadband is exceptionally spotty

item.title: The video that changed the narrative of a fatal beating on the border - Santa Barbara News-Press
item.description: Ashley Young became part of a growing legion to bear witness to state violence at the hands of U.S. immigration officials.

item.title: Ray Ford: Into the chaparral - Santa Barbara News-Press
item.description: What begins as an easy ramble up Cold Spring Canyon turns more serious as the creek narrows, the brush thickens and the trail remains stubbornly out of reach

item.description: The county Planning Commission on Wednesday will consider whether to approve a drive-thru proposed for the site of a shuttered IHOP restaurant, next to Starbucks

item.title: Inside the silicosis epidemic that’s killing countertop stonecutters: ‘My lungs had nothing left’ - Santa Barbara News-Press
item.description: A new California law aims to protect workers from silicosis, an incurable lung disease. Experts say it isn’t enough.

item.title: California sues Trump over order to open oil pipeline on Santa Barbara coast - Santa Barbara News-Press
item.description: The state is hoping to block what it says is an unprecedented power grab: using emergency authority to force the restart of an offshore oil operation.
